variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A multimodal mixture-of-experts (MoE) system processes more than one input type, such as text and images, while activating only a small part of a much larger model for each token. A learned router scores a pool of expert networks and sends each token to one or a few experts.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Top-1 routed
pairs.detail: Each token takes one selected expert path.
pairs.explanation: Each token takes one selected expert path. Active compute is predictable, but a hot expert has no second expert path unless the implementation defines one.

pairs.label: Top-k routed
pairs.detail: Each token activates several experts and combines their outputs.
pairs.explanation: Each token activates several experts and combines their outputs. This can add representation capacity while increasing dispatches, communication, and expert work.

pairs.label: Shared plus routed
pairs.detail: A shared expert processes every token while routed experts add conditional capacity.
pairs.explanation: A shared expert processes every token while routed experts add conditional capacity. The shared path can capture common behavior, but it is real compute, not a free fallback.

variants.hint:
Top-1 routed: Each token takes one selected expert path.

Top-k routed: Each token activates several experts and combines their outputs.

Shared plus routed: A shared expert processes every token while routed experts add conditional capacity.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Skip the sparse transform
pairs.detail: Preserves bounded expert work and latency, but removes conditional compute from the affected token.
pairs.explanation: Preserves bounded expert work and latency, but removes conditional compute from the affected token. Measure which modalities and evidence tokens are dropped.

pairs.label: Try another expert
pairs.detail: Can preserve sparse processing when spare capacity exists, but changes expert semantics, gate normalization, communication, and load on the fallback destination.
pairs.explanation: Can preserve sparse processing when spare capacity exists, but changes expert semantics, gate normalization, communication, and load on the fallback destination.

pairs.label: Use a shared path
pairs.detail: Provides a known general path when the architecture supports it.
pairs.explanation: Provides a known general path when the architecture supports it. It raises active compute and may become a new shared bottleneck during broad failures.

variants.prompt: What makes a model layer a sparse mixture of experts?
options: A router activates only a bounded subset of expert networks for each token.
Every token executes every expert and averages all outputs.
The service chooses one database for the whole request.
Image tokens bypass the model and are stored in a cache.
variants.explanation: Sparse MoE uses conditional computation: the router selects one or a few expert paths per token rather than executing the full expert pool.

Modality labels make expert capacity unlimited.

Text and image token counts are always equal.

All expert weights are deleted from memory.
The router automatically retrains itself during inference.
